quick: Renal, hepatic, hematologic on prolonged use
summary: Amoxycillin is a broad-spectrum aminopenicillin used for respiratory, ENT, urinary, skin and dental infections and as part of H. pylori eradication. Bactericidal via cell-wall synthesis inhibition. Main risk is hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis.
indications: Endocarditis prophylaxis for at-risk dental/surgical procedures

dosage.d: 25-45 mg/kg/day divided q12h or 20-40 mg/kg/day q8h

admin: Take with or without food; start of meal reduces GI upset
Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms improve
Shake oral suspension well before each dose
Maintain regular dosing intervals for consistent levels
Screen for penicillin/cephalosporin allergy before starting
moa: Inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), blocking transpeptidation/cross-linking of peptidoglycan. This produces a bactericidal effect against susceptible gram-positive and many gram-negative organisms.

relative: Severe renal impairment without dose adjustment

preg: Generally considered safe in pregnancy; widely used. Use when clearly needed.
lact: Excreted in breast milk in small amounts and considered compatible. Monitor infant for diarrhea, candidiasis or rash.
renal: Reduce dose or extend interval in significant impairment: CrCl 10-30 mL/min give 250-500 mg q12h; CrCl <10 mL/min give 250-500 mg q24h. Supplement after hemodialysis.
hepatic: Use with caution; rare cholestatic hepatitis reported (more with co-amoxiclav). Monitor liver function on prolonged therapy.

major: Allopurinol - increased incidence of skin rash
Methotrexate - reduced renal clearance, increased toxicity
moderate: Probenecid - increased amoxicillin levels (reduced tubular secretion)
minor: Oral contraceptives - possible reduced efficacy (advise backup)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food does not significantly impair absorption.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction tests; can affect estriol assays in pregnancy.

monitoring: Renal function on prolonged therapy or in impairment
Liver function and CBC during extended courses
Allergic reactions, especially early after first dose
counsel: Complete the entire course even if feeling better
Report rash, hives, swelling or difficulty breathing immediately
Report severe or bloody diarrhea (may occur weeks after)
Use additional contraception if on hormonal contraceptives
pk: Rapid absorption; bactericidal soon after dosing
Tablets/caps at room temp; reconstituted suspension refrigerate, discard after 14 days
pearls: First-line for acute otitis media and strep pharyngitis
Amoxicillin rash with mononucleosis does not equal true penicillin allergy
Better oral bioavailability and less frequent dosing than ampicillin
Key component of triple therapy for H. pylori
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule; do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose mainly causes GI symptoms and fluid/electrolyte imbalance. Crystalluria possible; maintain hydration. Treat supportively; amoxicillin is removed by hemodialysis.
